title: Singular-element witnesses in the height-zero auxiliary algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $A,C$ finitely presented commutative $R$-algebras, and $\Lambda$ a commutative $R$-algebra. Let $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$, $\beta:A\to C$, $\gamma:C\to\Lambda$ be $R$-algebra homomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] with $\gamma\beta=\alpha$. Let $s\subset A$ be a finite subset of $H_{A/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], $n:s\to\mathbb N$, and $\ell:s\to\Lambda$ with $\ell(a)\alpha(a)^{n(a)}=0$ for every $a\in s$. Let $c\in H_{C/R}$. Then there are a finitely presented $R$-algebra $B$ and maps $\beta\prime:A\to B$, $\delta:B\to\Lambda$ with $\delta\beta\prime=\alpha$, an element $b\in H_{B/R}$ with $\delta(b)=(\prod_{a\in s}\ell(a))\gamma(c)$, and, for every $a\in s$, an element $d_a\in H_{B/R}$ with $\delta(d_a)=\alpha(a)^{n(a)+1}$. The carrier of $C$ and of $B$ is taken in the maximum of the universes of $R,A$.

proof.text: If s is empty, use B=C, beta_prime=beta, delta=gamma, b=c. The empty product is one and the indexed assertion is vacuous.

proof.text: Otherwise s is a nonempty finite type. Equip C with its A-algebra structure via beta. Apply FinitePresentation.of_restrict_scalars_finitePresentation, then FinitePresentation.out and the finite-generator characterization of the kernel ideal to obtain k,m,f,q. Choose a polynomial p lifting c by surjectivity of the proved presentation map q.

proof.text: Construct the polynomial quotient B using PopescuAuxPoly and popescuAuxIdeal. Evaluate x through gamma q, y_i at alpha(a_i)^n_i, z at L=product ell_i, and t at zero. Each ell_i divides L, so hkill implies L*alpha(a_i)^n_i=0. Polynomial extensionality and gamma beta=alpha show that the f_j evaluate to zero. The quotient universal property gives delta; its composite with the structure map beta_prime is alpha.

proof.text: The polynomial ring P over A is finitely presented over R by FinitePresentation.mvPolynomial. It is Noetherian by FiniteType.isNoetherianRing, hence its defining ideal is finitely generated. Apply FinitePresentation.quotient to prove finite presentation of B.

proof.text: The given singular-ideal memberships make C_c and A_(a_i) smooth over R. Apply popescuAuxQuot_smooth_localizations to this explicit quotient and the finite presentation. The smooth elements z*p and a_i*y_i lie in the generating set of the singular ideal, hence in its radical. Evaluation gives delta(z*p)=L*gamma(c) and delta(a_i*y_i)=alpha(a_i)^(n_i+1). These are the required b and d_i.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_popescu_height_zero_auxiliary_witnesses
    {R : Type u} {A : Type v} {Λ : Type t} {C : Type (max u v)}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing Λ] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R Λ] [Algebra R C]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [FinitePresentation R A] [FinitePresentation R C]
    (α : A →ₐ[R] Λ) (β : A →ₐ[R] C) (γ : C →ₐ[R] Λ)
    (hcomp : γ.comp β = α) (s : Finset A)
    (hs : ∀ a ∈ s, a ∈ singularIdeal R A)
    (n : s → ℕ) (ell : s → Λ)
    (hkill : ∀ a : s, ell a * α a.val ^ n a = 0)
    (c : C) (hc : c ∈ singularIdeal R C) :
    ∃ (B : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra R B),
      ∃ (β' : A →ₐ[R] B) (δ : B →ₐ[R] Λ),
        FinitePresentation R B ∧ δ.comp β' = α ∧
        (∃ b ∈ singularIdeal R B, δ b = (∏ a : s, ell a) * γ c) ∧
        (∀ a : s, ∃ d ∈ singularIdeal R B, δ d = α a.val ^ (n a + 1))
